facts.text: Ahuntsic’s oldest church, La Visitation-de-la-Bienheureuse-Vierge-Marie, dates back to 1750 and still stands as Montreal’s oldest surviving church.
The name Ahuntsic comes from a Huron nickname for a Frenchman who arrived in New France around 1619, a detail uncovered by recent historical research.
Ahuntsic was founded as an independent village on January 21, 1897, before being annexed to Montreal in 1910.
The area’s early economy relied on milling and agriculture along the Rivière des Prairies, with mill remnants still visible today.
Ahuntsic hosts the Collège Ahuntsic, a prominent CEGEP that attracts students from across the city.
The neighborhood is known for its green spaces, including the revitalized Ahuntsic Park and the nearby L'Île-de-la-Visitation Nature Park.
